svg.aria-label: The rebuilt shell with every region tagged as either inline or resource-backed. The tag names the source a region reads, not how long its content lives: resource-backed regions subscribe to a standing collection, inline regions render from the session's own item stream. Both survive a reload, because those items are persisted. The left rail is entirely resource-backed: the org and team badge, the channel list, and the seat list each subscribe to a collection. The centre column is mixed: its channel header, showing members and boards, is resource-backed, while the turn stream, the task updates and the approval cards are all inline, rendering from the session's item stream, so earlier turns and already-resolved approvals are still there after a reload. The prompt input is neither — it is a control. The right panel is entirely resource-backed: the board columns subscribe to the channel's board ledger, and the roster subscribes to the seat inventory. The roster's home is this panel; the rail carries the seat list, which is navigation into it. A key on the right records that the split is not new: it already exists in the code today, unnamed. Resource-backed today means useResourceCollectionList on the artifacts collection, useClientData, and useSession on a child session inside the background-work panel. Inline today means the Conversation and ConversationContent components, the request-group renderer, TaskPlan, and every renderer under the flow-state folder. The key names TaskPlan as the seam to watch, because it renders task-change and task-board-meta items inline today and its own file header says a board-style layout is a per-app concern — which is exactly the resource-backed sibling this epic ships. A closing note says spine item 3 moves both shapes into the client packages rather than inventing them, that the split is a source and never a lifetime, and that a region whose shape cannot be expressed as a package export is a design finding for FIX-1477's spec, not a licence to leave it in the app.

svg.text: Spine item 3 moves both shapes into the client packages. It does not invent them — it names what the app already does in two ways.
A region whose shape cannot be expressed as a package export is a design finding for FIX-1477’s spec, not a reason to leave it in the app (ER-4).
Both shapes survive a reload. The split is which source a region reads — the session’s item stream, or a standing collection — never how long its content lives (D5).
